summary.headline: Supreme Industries Q1 FY27 revenue rose 4% to INR2,718 crore on 14% volume decline, with standalone PAT up 17% to INR208 crore; FY27 guidance held.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 volumes fell about 14% to 1,57,536 tons, but revenue grew 4% to INR2,718 crore as value-added products rose 22% to INR1,142 crore. Standalone operating profit rose 25% to INR398 crore and PAT rose 17% to INR208 crore, helped by lower-margin agri pipe volumes falling sharply. Management attributed the weakness to April 2026 polymer price volatility and channel destocking, and said volumes recovered in May-July. Management maintained FY27 guidance of 12-13% overall volume growth, 15-17% piping volume growth and 14-14.5% EBITDA margin, plus about INR1,000 crore capex.

financial_highlights.change: Derived: 398/2,718; not stated on call as a figure
vs 8.8% in June 2025 quarter (as cited by analyst, not disputed)

segments.name: Plastic piping systems
segments.commentary: Volume fell about 15% YoY with value flat; April 2026 volume reportedly down more than 50%, with May-July showing growth. Agri pipe and polythene pipe saw the sharpest declines; PVC pipe demand also fell.

segments.name: Packaging
segments.commentary: Volume down about 10% YoY, value up 9%. Management attributed the value gain to customised, higher-realisation solutions.

segments.name: Industrial products
segments.commentary: Volume down about 6% YoY, value up 24%; OEM demand tied to end-market (e.g., air conditioners), priced on cost-plus. Value gain attributed to product mix (pellets, dustbins).

segments.name: Consumer products
segments.commentary: Volume down about 22% YoY, value down 11%.

segments.name: Composite cylinders
segments.commentary: Capacity 9-10 lakh cylinders per annum; utilisation 25-35%. HPCL tender of 2 lakh pieces; LOI for 60,000 pieces, supply from next month.

segments.name: Wavin (acquired) and Gas piping
segments.commentary: Wavin capacity about 70,000 tons, 50-60% utilised in Q1; management targets about 70% for the year. Gas piping (pipe and fitting) business seen at about INR600 crore this year; orders already supplied.

guidance_outlook: Overall volume growth 12-13% for FY27 (maintained from April 2026 guidance).
Piping volume growth 15-17% for FY27, maintained; management said it refers to the full year, not the balance nine months.
EBITDA margin 14-14.5% for FY27, maintained; management said FY28-29 not discussed.
Capex of about INR1,000 crore for FY27 maintained; INR500 crore committed so far, depending on machine arrival.
Management expects growth in H1 FY27 and in Q2 FY27, which it said would be visible in October.
Exports: target USD150 million in 6-7 years from USD26 million last year.
capex_capacity: Windows and doors (uPVC) business: INR220 crore invested; revenue potential INR300-350 crore at normal utilisation; capacity 5,000 tons per year; production started and market sales begun, with better utilisation expected next year.
New plants planned at Bihar (21 acres) and Jammu (13 acres) to together exceed 50,000 tons in about two years, built in small phases.
Malanpur facility to make material handling products (crates, pallets).
Pondicherry: existing factory product for Whirlpool to be shifted; capacity to be added for furniture exports. Erode land acquisition in progress.
OPVC: new machine for Eastern India; some machines running in Western India. CPVC market share said to have risen.
Composite cylinders: 9-10 lakh per annum capacity, utilisation 25-35%.
demand_pricing: April 2026 polymer price volatility caused channel destocking; management said inventory is now being refilled and demand is coming in, with PVC up INR9/kg recently.
Management said agri demand restarts from mid-September, with robust demand expected through to March as reservoirs fill.

PVC prices stabilised after about 20 April; MIP (minimum import price) for suspension-grade PVC resin set at USD766 per ton, with management noting it sets a floor, not a ceiling. MIP reportedly for six months.
Management said no inventory gain or loss to quantify; said pipe is low-margin and its volume fall lifted blended margin.
Pricing: management said prices track raw material costs, and the company is focused on return on capital employed rather than margin expansion.
Industry-wide plastic de-growth; management had no industry volume data.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 15-17% piping volume guidance for the full year, given a weak Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it refers to the full year and is maintained; it cited excellent July growth and expected good Q2 growth, to be seen in October. April volume was down more than 50%, with May-July showing growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 EBITDA guidance 14-14.5% when Q1 margin was 14.6% and earlier guidance was higher?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not guiding lower; Q1 margin rose because pipe demand fell. It called the guidance conservative and said it does not want to present a rosy picture.

qa_highlights.question: Was there any inventory gain in Q1, or any in Q2 from the July PVC price rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify or confirm either inventory gains or losses, saying it would discuss at year-end if anything happens.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 14% margin improvement from mix persist, and what is the outlook for Wavin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Wavin is running at about 70% utilisation, with margins in the same range as Supreme; it said the 14-14.5% margin guidance holds.

qa_highlights.question: How big can gas piping be, and what is the status of uPVC windows?
qa_highlights.answer: Gas piping (pipe and fitting) was estimated at about INR600 crore this year, with orders supplied. Windows: INR220 crore invested, revenue potential INR300-350 crore at normal utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Will lost volumes be recovered, and is there a restocking effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said lost volume will be recovered, with growth in H1 FY27; it said channel is refilling inventory now and there is no destocking.

risks_watch: Piping volume guidance of 15-17% for FY27 needs roughly 25%+ growth over the balance nine months after a 15% Q1 decline; July growth and Q2 growth are unquantified until October.

PVC and polymer price path after the MIP (USD766/ton, six months) and July PVC increase of INR9/kg; management said prices can still rise and the MIP is a floor, so inventory gain or loss exposure is unquantified.
Margin sustainability: Q1 EBITDA margin of 14.6% came from lower-margin pipe volume falling; management guides 14-14.5% for FY27 and said the mix benefit should normalise over the year.
Agri demand timing: management says demand restarts mid-September, so H2 pipe recovery depends on the season and reservoir filling; April volumes fell more than 50%.
Wavin ramp-up (70,000 tons capacity, 50-60% utilised in Q1, target about 70%) and capex execution (INR500 crore committed of about INR1,000 crore, dependent on machine arrival).
Composite cylinder utilisation at 25-35% with order-driven flow; HPCL LOI for 60,000 pieces with supply from August.
key_quotes: We maintain the same volume growth guidance.
We are talking for the whole year.
We are not guiding lower margin.
Lost volume will be recovered, and we will have growth in the first half.
Nothing to report either on inventory gain or inventory loss. If anything happens, we'll be talking end of the year.
summary.management_tone: Confident on medium-term demand and the full-year guidance, but cautious and evasive on near-term specifics. Management declined to quantify industry volumes, inventory gains or losses, and FY28-29 margins, and repeatedly said it would discuss only FY27 or year-end.

adds.what: Windows and doors (uPVC) business, 5,000 tons per year capacity (INR220 crore invested)
New plants at Bihar (21 acres) and Jammu (13 acres) to together exceed 50,000 tons
Composite cylinders existing capacity 9-10 lakh cylinders per annum (utilisation 25-35%); HPCL LOI for 60,000 pieces

growth.why: Management maintained FY27 overall volume growth guidance of 12-13% (piping 15-17%) and 14-14.5% EBITDA margin, with ~INR1,000 crore capex; backing is partial, with Wavin utilisation targeting ~70%, the Bihar/Jammu plants (50,000+ tons in about two years), an LOI for 60,000 composite cylinders, and expected growth in Q2 FY27 but Q1 volumes fell 14%.
